title: Gender inequality is being reproduced across poverty, conflict, food security, digital access, care, and institutional power
source_unit: UN Women and UN DESA, Progress on the Sustainable Development Goals: The Gender Snapshot 2025
geography: Global comparison across the 2030 Agenda, with gender-disaggregated indicators and scenario analysis

denominator.unit: women and girls worldwide under the report's poverty scenarios

women_girls_extreme_poverty_2030.unit: millions of women and girls projected to remain in extreme poverty in 2030 if current trends continue

digital_divide_gdp_gain.unit: trillion US dollars of additional global GDP by 2030 under a closed gender digital divide scenario

women_girls_benefit_digital_closure.unit: millions of women and girls projected to benefit from closing the gender digital divide

women_lifted_from_poverty_digital_closur.unit: millions of women projected to be lifted from poverty by 2050 under the digital-divide scenario

observations.method: UN Women and UN DESA synthesis of SDG indicators and modeled scenario analysis linking gender equality investments, digital inclusion, and poverty outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The projection is scenario-dependent and does not identify a single causal intervention; global aggregates conceal country, age, disability, household, and intersectional variation.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, men and boys, poor households, digitally excluded populations, and countries across income and development contexts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital access can expand opportunity while leaving affordability, safety, care, skills, ownership, and bargaining gaps intact; GDP gains do not automatically become income, security, or agency gains.

denominator.unit: global population and conflict/food-security indicators summarized by the report

women_girls_near_deadly_conflict.unit: millions of women and girls living within reach of deadly conflict

female_male_food_insecurity_gap.unit: millions more female adults than male adults experiencing moderate or severe food insecurity in 2024

gender_equality_targets.value: none of the global gender-equality targets are on track
gender_equality_targets.unit: report assessment of SDG gender-equality targets

observations.method: UN Women and UN DESA compilation of conflict exposure, food-security, and SDG progress indicators with gender disaggregation.
observations.uncertainty: Conflict proximity, food insecurity, and target-status measures use different reference periods and reporting systems; they describe exposure and progress status rather than individual harm or causal pathways.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls in conflict-affected settings, female and male adults facing food insecurity, displaced and otherwise exposed populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Gender gaps may widen through conflict and food shocks, but local institutions, social networks, humanitarian access, and women-led responses can change exposure and recovery trajectories.

denominator.unit: global SDG gender-equality indicator and policy evidence frame

care_and_work.value: unpaid care, decent work, social protection, and economic resources remain central cross-SDG gender constraints

institutional_backing.value: progress depends on financing, data, services, legal reform, and accountable institutions rather than isolated empowerment programs

investment_frame.value: targeted investments in women and girls can produce gains across poverty, food, climate, digital inclusion, and public decision-making

observations.method: Cross-SDG synthesis of gender-disaggregated indicators and policy recommendations from UN Women and UN DESA.
observations.uncertainty: The synthesis joins indicators with different definitions, coverage, and time frames; recommended investments are not evaluated as a single causal package.
observations.subgroup: Caregivers, workers in formal and informal employment, women and girls needing social protection, and institutions responsible for services and data.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal legal or budget commitments may not translate into accessible services, changed household bargaining, safer work, or durable institutional power.

power_distribution.value: women remain underrepresented in the institutions that shape economic, political, peace, security, technology, and public-life decisions

implementation_gap.value: the report identifies an urgent gap between commitments and implementation across gender-equality targets

data_requirement.value: gender-disaggregated data and sustained financing are required to monitor progress and target action

observations.method: UN Women and UN DESA review of SDG indicators, institutional conditions, financing, and policy implementation barriers.
observations.uncertainty: Representation and legal indicators do not directly measure influence, safety, enforcement, or lived access; country reporting and data availability are uneven.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, women-led organizations, public institutions, political and economic decision-makers, and communities affected by implementation gaps.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional representation can matter without producing immediate parity, while local collective action may generate change that global indicators register slowly.

related_sources.claim: WEF Global Gender Gap 2026 provides a complementary parity-index and leadership-pipeline lens.
UN Women provides complementary institutional and social-norms analysis.

boundary: This record adds an SDG-wide gender-inequality route linking poverty, conflict, food insecurity, digital access, care, work, rights, and institutional power. It uses aggregate publication indicators and scenarios, not respondent-level analysis, household microdata, individual conflict histories, or causal estimates of any single intervention.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN Women, UN DESA, and UN SDG publication pages and the 2025 Gender Snapshot PDF were checked for the poverty, digital-divide, conflict, food-insecurity, implementation, and institutional-power claims.
